_register: Formal « u » (never « je ») in sentences addressed to the reader; buttons, menu entries and step lists use the infinitive (Uitlenen, Opslaan, De barcode scannen); no jokes, no exclamation marks; neutral between the Netherlands and Flanders.
_quotes: Double quotation marks “text” (as in the English messages), no space inside them; no space before : ; ? !; decimal comma, thousands separated by a point or a thin space; dates as dd-mm-yyyy; compounds are written closed (« leerlingenlijst »), with a hyphen only where Dutch spelling requires it (« back-up », « e-mailadres », « PDF-bestand »); the arrow → stays.
_plural: Two forms (one, other); a noun after a number is plural (« 2 boeken ») except units that stay singular (« 5 euro », « 3 mm »); « 0 boeken » takes the plural.

copy.note: One physical copy with its own barcode; never « kopie ».

record.note: Catalogue entry of a title, as in Dutch and Flemish library systems; the short form « titel » is allowed in buttons and where the context is clear. « record » alone is avoided as an anglicism.

patron.note: Usual word in Dutch and Flemish libraries (plural « leners »); « gebruiker » is too general. Gender-neutral in practice.

card.note: Short form « pas » where the context is clear; Flemish libraries say « lenerskaart », both are understood, one is used everywhere.

loan.note: The act and the lending; the area of the program is « Uitleen » and the verb « uitlenen ». « lening » is avoided (it means a money loan).

return.note: The action: « Inname » on the menu, « terugbrengen » for a patron's act and « innemen » or « de inname registreren » for the verb in the desk's actions.

renew.note: Extending the due date; used in all Dutch and Flemish libraries, never « vernieuwen ».

reminder.note: The printed slip asking for the return; « aanmaning » is too harsh for pupils.

call number.note: The shelf mark on the spine (B 4 DEL, 590 ROS). « plaatsnummer » is used in Flanders and is understood; « signatuur » is the library term in both countries. Explained in the tooltip.

spine band.note: The coloured band with pictogram and signatuur on the spine; not « rugetiket », so that it is not confused with the barcode « etiket ».

label.note: An adhesive label; « sticker » is not used.

barcode.note: As in Dutch and Flemish library software; « streepjescode » is not used. Plural « barcodes ».

class.note: A school class (3 B); plural « klassen ».

group.note: Used for a group of teachers; not the Dutch primary-school « groep » (a class).

reading level.note: The school year a book is meant for; not the AVI levels.

classification.note: The sorting scheme (Dewey for non-fiction); « indeling » is the plain word for the order on the shelf.

catalogue.note: Plural « catalogi »; written « catalogus », never « catalogue ».

stocktaking.note: Checking the shelves against the catalogue; the verb is « inventariseren ».

wish list.note: Books a patron would like the library to have.

census.note: Registering the leners with their photo; the verb « registreren ».

class upgrade.note: Moving every class up a year at the end of the school year; the verb phrase is « de klassen doorschuiven ».

staff account.note: « personeelsaccount » is also correct; one is used everywhere.

backup.note: Official Dutch spelling with a hyphen; plural « back-ups ».

restore.note: The action: « een back-up terugzetten »; the noun is « herstel (n.) » (e.g. the heading of the restore page).

print list.note: A list of leners or exemplaren to print cards or labels for.

scanner.note: The USB barcode reader that types like a keyboard; « scanner » alone where the context is clear.

wizard.note: The first-start sequence of questions; « installatiewizard » in full, « wizard » in short.

student.note: Plural « leerlingen »; « student » is for higher education only.

teacher.note: Neutral between the Netherlands (« docent », « leraar ») and Flanders (« leerkracht »); plural « leerkrachten ».

administration.note: The administration area of a program; « administratie » is the office work.

configuration.note: The settings as a whole; a single setting is « instelling ».

return desk / circulation desk.note: The desk where loans and returns are handled; the area as a whole is « Uitleen ».
